nodes.description: MED12 disease variants alter recruitment of the MED12-containing complex to immediate early gene (JUN, FOS, EGR1) promoters, producing variant- and cell-type-specific changes in their expression. Downstream, late responsive genes are dysregulated, including the RE1-silencing transcription factor (REST/NRSF), a master repressor of neuron-specific genes, disrupting neural plasticity and neuronal gene programs. MED12 also regulates Wnt/β-catenin and Sonic hedgehog (via GLI3) developmental signaling.

nodes.description: MED12 is a subunit of the CDK8 kinase module (MED12, MED13, Cyclin C, and CDK8), a dissociable regulatory module of the Mediator complex that modulates RNA polymerase II transcription. MED12 activates CDK8 kinase activity by wrapping around CDK8 via a conserved T-loop interaction. Disease-associated missense variants alter MED12 function within this module rather than abolishing the protein, consistent with the observation that only a small subset of MED12 variants produces the distinct MED12-related syndromes.
